title: Ito capability protocol
description: What Ito's server and a capability say to each other. The server starts each capability as its own process and they exchange JSON-RPC 2.0 messages, one JSON object per line, on the capability's standard input and output; the `jsonrpc` member is left out, as in Codex's app server. Standard error is the capability's log. A capability exits when its standard input closes.

ProtocolVersion.description: The capability protocol's version, as `MAJOR.MINOR`. Until 1.0 the server and a capability must speak the same `0.MINOR`.

InitializeParams.description: `initialize`, from the server, first after starting the process.

InitializeResult.description: The answer to `initialize`: the capability's protocol version and its manifest.

Manifest.description: Everything the server needs to show, set up and offer a capability, as data.

id.description: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes; it names the capability's commands (`ito <id> …`), folder and endpoints.

version.description: The capability's own version, as `MAJOR.MINOR`, which apps use to decide whether they know its screen.

kind.description: `domain` for a topic of your life, `hand` for a way to act that isn't one.

title.description: Its name in Settings, such as Reports.

symbol.description: An SF Symbol name for apps to show beside it, such as `exclamationmark.bubble`.

summary.description: One sentence on what it does, for Settings and for the agent.

setup.description: The fields of its setup sheet, in order.

operations.description: What the agent can do with it.

skill.description: Markdown the agent reads before using it: when and how. The server adds a reference of its commands.

uses.description: What it reaches beyond its own folder, shown before you switch it on.

Field.description: One field of a setup sheet. A `secret` goes to the server once and never comes back to any app.

optional.description: True when the capability can run without it.

Operation.description: One thing the agent can do. Every operation is a command, `ito <capability> <name>`; with `tool`, it is also one of the agent's tools.

title.description: What it does, as a tool's title.

running.description: Its step's title while it runs, such as Reporting it to Ito.

done.description: Its step's title once it has run, such as Reported it to Ito.

description.description: When and how to use it, for the agent.

input.description: A JSON Schema object for its input; each property becomes a `--flag` of its command.

tool.description: The tool's name, when the operation is also one of the agent's tools.

publishes.description: True when its input ends up in public, so the server removes your secret answers from it first.

Values.description: Setup values by field name: a string for `text`, `secret` and `choice`, a boolean for `toggle`.

StartParams.description: `start`, from the server, when the capability is on and set up: its values, its own secrets among them, and its private folder, which is also its working directory. An error answer shows the capability as needing you, with the error's message.

CheckParams.description: `check`, from the server, to test setup values before they're saved; it may come before `start`.

CheckResult.description: The answer to `check`: nothing when the values work, otherwise what's wrong, in plain words.

CallParams.description: `call`, from the server, to run an operation. An error answer's message goes to the agent.

turn.description: The turn the agent is in, when there is one.

CallResult.description: The answer to `call`: text for the agent, and optionally the same as data.

CancelParams.description: `cancel`, a notification from the server: stop working on the `call` with this request id, and answer it with an error.

StatusParams.description: `status`, a notification from the capability: whether it's working, or needs you, and why.

detail.description: What's wrong, such as GitHub rejected the token.
